I saved the Q3 results to `answer.json`. Run the same way on Q2, my query reproduces every one of the 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment by net sales | smb, 316,534,383 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Top category by net sales | svc, 312,755,660 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u93@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 240 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 692,548 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -3.3% |

The Q2 values only matched once I made three adjustments to the data:
- **Time zone:** order times are stored in UTC, so I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before assigning months and quarters.
- **Segment names:** labels like `SMB`/`smb` and `consumer` with a leading space were merged by lowercasing and trimming spaces.
- **Duplicate customers:** there are 300 customer IDs but only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f I counted each email as one customer.

STATUS: DONE
